topic: How should the sk-create-chart mode chart templates and delivered output improve, measured against what the best open-source charting libraries produce? READ FIRST: .opencode/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-chart/SKILL.md, references/template-contract.md, references/catalog.md, references/color-system.md, scripts/check-corpus.cjs, and every file under assets/templates/. Study Chart.js, D3, Vega-Lite, Plotly, Observable Plot and ECharts: what a delivered chart from each actually looks like, and what conventions they share about axis ladders and tick selection, label and legend placement, colour ramps, accessibility (contrast, non-colour encoding, screen-reader affordances), responsive sizing, and the relationship between data and mark. Report where this corpus falls short of those conventions and where it is already ahead, citing file:line in the corpus and a named upstream source for every claim. CONSTRAINTS: every recommendation must reconcile with the mode contract that a template is one self-contained HTML file opening on a double click with no build step, no package manager and no remote dependency (references/template-contract.md sections 3 to 6) — say explicitly how a recommended library or technique satisfies that or why it cannot. Only MIT-class open-source projects may be used as sources of ideas or code; this repository is MIT and public. Do NOT open, read, search or reference any reference-implementation clone under any scratch, tmp or vendor directory: it is PolyForm Noncommercial and nothing from it may be copied or paraphrased. Deliver ranked actionable recommendations, each marked as template-level change (applyable now) or contract-level change (needs a decision).
